name: Khaus
backstory: One of Gorff's keepers of record, maintains the city's own written account of the tollhouse, the temple, and the Salthos house's claim to the crossing.

experience.text: Heard that Auroboro and Mekestros now have a child, Mekoboro.
Had a child with Aurebalo, named Khaubalo.
Heard that Auroboro and Aurebalo now have a child, Aureboro.
Heard that Mekestros and Aureluko now have a child, Mekaluko.
Had a child with Mekoboro, named Khaoboro.
Heard that Khaubalo and Mekestros now have a child, Khaubestro.

criterion.standard: counts his own city's account reconciled above one more year of an unexplained gap nobody in Gorff has to answer for
criterion.wasted_life: keeping a record honest enough to embarrass his own city, then letting the one figure that would actually prove it go unchecked for three years
criterion.derivation: collision between his backstory (Gorff's own keeper of record) and the sample's own toll_ledger_arrears (a live, unreconciled discrepancy in the exact accounts he maintains)
criterion.trusts: a story that's been carried and retold and still holds together
criterion.distrusts: a record that insists on a precision no one who was actually there ever needed

previous.standard: counts an account that could embarrass his own city above one that only flatters it
previous.wasted_life: keeping a record that only ever confirms what Gorff already believed
previous.origin: collision between his backstory (keeps Gorff's own written account) and CONFLICT-03 itself

history.note: re-derived after encodings.json gained three new concrete concepts (crossing_market_roof, toll_ledger_arrears, forliamus_betrothal_offer) via /tell, at the author's explicit direction, to diversify arcs away from the epistemic-conflict default

routines.routine_actions: works out of the temple's own records annex through the morning, cross-checks new claims against the ledger before entering anything as settled, avoids being drawn into the square's arguments

arc.premise: With the reconciled toll figure finally agreed in principle, Khaus wants it entered as a formally cross-signed record in Gorff's own ledger - both sides' clerks putting their names to the same number - so it can't quietly come undone the moment either city needs it to. A record only he vouches for isn't the kind that survives being checked.
